summary:
Hymn of Jörð is an interactive project that transforms real environmental data into sound experiences through sonification. We developed a JavaScript application that uses different instruments and musical characteristics to represent environmental variables such as temperature, humidity, CO₂ concentration, light intensity, and the amount of Arctic ice.

The system converts environmental values into musical notes, frequencies, intensities, and musical variations. Each variable has its own sound identity, allowing users to distinguish between them while they are played individually or together. Additionally, it incorporates dissonance effects to highlight environmental anomalies, such as unusual increases in CO₂ concentration.

The project aims to provide an alternative and intuitive way to explore scientific information, allowing environmental changes to be perceived not only visually but also through sound. This offers new ways to interpret information about the state of our planet and raise environmental awareness.
details:
Project Details

Hymn of Jörð is an interactive application that transforms environmental data into music through a process known as sonification. It works by processing and normalizing different environmental variables, such as temperature, humidity, CO₂ concentration, light intensity, and the amount of Arctic ice, converting their values into musical characteristics such as frequencies, pitches, intensities, and rhythms.

The application allows users to play each variable independently or combine them to create a musical composition that represents different aspects of the planet's condition. It also incorporates an anomaly detection system that generates an alarm through musical dissonance. When a variable behaves outside its established parameters, a dissonant note is introduced, disrupting the harmony of the composition. This change represents an environmental problem in the corresponding area that requires attention and corrective action.

One of its main benefits is providing an alternative way to interpret scientific information, allowing users to identify environmental changes and anomalies through sound rather than relying exclusively on graphs or statistics. Its intended impact is to promote environmental awareness and encourage people to better understand the changes affecting our planet.

To develop the project, we used JavaScript and HTML, along with Tone.js as our audio generation and playback engine. We also used Visual Studio Code as our development environment and scientific data from sources such as NOAA, including CO₂ records from Mauna Loa.

The creative aspect of the project lies in using musical harmony as a representation of environmental balance. Music symbolizes a planet in a healthy state, while dissonance represents a disruption of that balance. In this way, the project aims to communicate that every environmental variable is part of an interconnected system and that problems in any of its components can affect the harmony of the whole.

During development, our team considered data accuracy, variable normalization, anomaly detection, the distinct sound representation of each layer, and ease of interaction. Our goal is to combine science, technology, and music to communicate the environmental condition of our planet in an original, accessible, and interactive way.
